paper_title: Air-Stable Manganese(I)-Catalyzed C–H Activation for Decarboxylative C–H/C–O Cleavages in Water
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2017 - Wang - Air‐Stable Manganese I ‐Catalyzed C H Activation for Decarboxylative C H C O Cleavages in/auto/Angew Chem Int Ed - 2017 - Wang - Air‐Stable Manganese I ‐Catalyzed C H Activation for Decarboxylative C H C O Cleavages in.md

knowledge_points.content: Manganese(I) catalysis using MnBr(CO)5 enables decarboxylative C–H/C–O functionalization for the synthesis of allylated indoles, arenes, and amino acids.
knowledge_points.evidence: The versatile C–H allylation occurred by facile organometallic C–H metalation on indoles, arenes, amino acids and synthetically meaningful aryl ketimines... Control experiments verified the essential role of the MnBr(CO)5 catalyst.

knowledge_points.content: The manganese(I)-catalyzed C–H functionalization is robust enough to occur efficiently in ambient air and using water (H2O) as the reaction medium.
knowledge_points.evidence: The manganese(I)-catalyzed C–H/C–O functionalization was not only tolerant to H2O, but occurred efficiently in an atmosphere of ambient air as well... with a high catalytic performance even at 60 °C when using H2O as the reaction medium.

knowledge_points.content: Optimization of the manganese(I) catalytic system in water under air reached yields as high as 95% for the allylation of 2-phenylpyridine with dioxolanone.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 1, entry 14: MnBr(CO)5, NaOAc, H2O, Under air, 100 °C, 16 h, Yield 95%, E/Z 5.9.

knowledge_points.content: Vinylated dioxolanones serve as effective coupling partners for manganese-catalyzed C–H functionalization, allowing for the introduction of secondary and tertiary allylic alcohol moieties.
knowledge_points.evidence: Subsequently, a representative set of vinylated dioxolanones 2 was probed... the manganese(I)-catalyzed C–H activation efficiently delivered the secondary and tertiary allylic alcohols 3ab–3af.

knowledge_points.content: Manganese(I)-catalyzed C–H activation exhibits a minor preference for electron-deficient arenes as demonstrated by intermolecular competition experiments.
knowledge_points.evidence: First, intermolecular competition experiments between electronically differentiated arenes revealed a minor preference for electron-deficient substrates.

knowledge_points.content: Mechanistic studies using D2O labeling confirm that the manganese(I)-catalyzed C–H metalation step is reversible and water-tolerant.
knowledge_points.evidence: Second, C–H activations in the presence of isotopically labeled D2O clearly revealed the reversible nature of a water-tolerant organometallic C–H activation elementary step (Scheme 4 a).

knowledge_points.content: The MnBr(CO)5 catalytic system demonstrates high functional group tolerance, including compatibility with chloro, bromo, iodo, hydroxyl, ester, and enolizable ketone substituents.
knowledge_points.evidence: Thereby, a set of synthetically useful electrophilic functional groups, including chloro, bromo, iodo, hydroxyl, ester, and enolizable ketone substituents, was fully tolerated.

knowledge_points.content: The active catalytic cycle involves an independently isolable organometallic complex (complex 4) that is competent in both catalytic and stoichiometric C–H/C–O functionalization.
knowledge_points.evidence: Third, the independently prepared organometallic complex 4 proved to be competent in both catalytic C–H/C–O functionalization (Scheme 4 b) as well as within its stoichiometric transformation (Scheme 4 c).

knowledge_points.content: Manganese(I) catalysis allows for the direct modification of amino acids under racemization-free conditions, which is critical for maintaining molecular chirality in bio-related optoelectronic applications.
knowledge_points.evidence: Finally, the synthetic utility of the C–H/C–O functionalization was exploited for the direct modification of amino acids 5, notably under racemization-free reaction conditions (Scheme 5 a).

knowledge_points.content: Sodium acetate (NaOAc) is a critical additive for the manganese(I)-catalyzed decarboxylative C–H activation; other additives like K2CO3 or amines significantly reduce catalytic efficacy.
knowledge_points.evidence: The use of additives other than NaOAc proved to be detrimental to the catalytic efficacy (entries 15–17). ... K2CO3 (entry 15) <10% yield.

knowledge_points.content: In the functionalization of aryl ketimines, the site-selectivity of the manganese catalyst is primarily controlled by steric interactions, with fluorine substituents providing secondary electronic control.
knowledge_points.evidence: The site-selectivity was found largely controlled by steric interactions, while the fluoro-group exerted a secondary effect to furnish ketone 8i and 8k as the sole product.
